craft_claim: Comic scenes intensify by repeating and heightening one rule or game beat by beat, rather than by adding unrelated jokes.

supporting_evidence.location: Concepts of 'game' and 'heightening' in long-form improvisation
supporting_evidence.note: Practitioner framework: a scene identifies a pattern or game and then heightens it by escalation, concentrating rather than dispersing the comic energy. Tier 4 practitioner support.
Escalation works because each beat re-establishes an expectation that the next turn violates, consistent with incongruity-resolution.

counterevidence.note: Unbroken escalation without substance can crowd out the main point; heightening must serve the piece's purpose.

scope: Scene and section construction in fiction, screen, and long-form prose.
exceptions: Sketch or absurdist forms may deliberately refuse escalation and hold a single static absurdity.
Comic relief passages that must stay brief should not heighten to a full comic climax.
